source_name: CBCG — Strateški plan 2025–2028
why_relevant: Forward-looking statement of what capabilities CBCG intends to build (typically payments modernisation, supervision capacity, EU alignment) — predicts the hiring and unit creation that will later appear as vacancies.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro — employee LinkedIn profiles (no confirmed company page)
why_relevant: For the smallest licensed banks (Ziraat, Zapad) no LinkedIn company page surfaced; individual employee profiles are then the only professional-network visibility into their staffing and org units.

source_name: RE:D Montenegro conference (Web Media Grupa / bankar.me / HESA Group with EBRD)
why_relevant: New Montenegrin real-estate-and-finance conference co-organised by the bankar.me publisher with EBRD partnership. Real estate is where mortgage-lending and corporate-banking executives appear on panels, so the speaker list is a title registry for bank lending leadership. Observed speakers include Vasilije Jaukovic (Associate Director and Senior Banker, EBRD) and Milovan Novakovic (CEO & Partner, Colliers Montenegro).

source_name: Tomorrow Conference (Montenegro) — founder/organiser and speaker programme
why_relevant: Montenegrin business/technology conference brand (founder and director Mladjen Merdovic, per a bankar.me interview). Cross-sector conferences of this type routinely put bank digital and marketing leadership on stage with current titles, and their sponsor walls indicate which banks and payment vendors are spending locally.

source_name: CFO Asocijacija Crne Gore (Association of Financial Directors) — newly formed AMM offshoot
why_relevant: A brand-new body enumerating the CFOs of Montenegrin institutions including banks — the CFO layer is exactly where finance-function hiring and reorganisation shows up first, and the founding board (Ivaštinović/Erste, Cmiljanić/Razvojna banka, Vujović/Addiko) is a ready-made contact map. As a new association it has no stable homepage found yet; track via AMM and trade press.

source_name: Startup Index Crne Gore coverage (DAN — tehnologije)
why_relevant: First comprehensive Montenegrin startup index (NTP + Game Changer Montenegro, 65 startups) — baseline population and headcount/growth signals for fintech-adjacent startups; national daily also runs tech-desk pieces on appointments.

entity_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore
source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala — annual report on the capital market
why_relevant: Annual regulator report enumerates licensed entities, licence decisions and enforcement over the year — a compact retrospective ground truth for reconciling a year of entity/leadership changes.

source_name: Portal eUprava Crne Gore — supervisory approval e-services
why_relevant: Government e-services catalogue documenting the fit-and-proper application procedures (what a candidate for a board member / executive director must file, which body decides, in what timeframe). Explains the administrative pipeline behind every approval, so it dates and sequences the signals collected elsewhere. A CBCG service entry also exists.

source_name: EBRD news releases on Montenegro banking transactions
why_relevant: Signing announcements explicitly name senior executives on both sides (e.g. EBRD VP Banking Matteo Patrone and CKB Management Board Chair Tamas Kamarasi), making them a reliable, dated record of who currently chairs Montenegrin bank management boards.

source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents (PSD) — Montenegro bank projects, incl. Montenegrin-language versions
why_relevant: PSDs name the client bank (e.g. Addiko banka AD Podgorica), the sponsor/ownership structure and the business rationale; the Montenegrin-language versions confirm official local naming of institutions, useful for entity resolution and for detecting new banking counterparties (a proxy for organisational change).

source_name: EBRD Country Strategy for Montenegro (2026–2031 draft and predecessors)
why_relevant: Country strategies diagnose banking-sector structure, state ownership, governance weaknesses and institutional capacity of the CBCG — an outside baseline against which organisational change can be measured.

source_name: Portal Analitika / RTCG — Montenegrin general media banking coverage
why_relevant: Mainstream Montenegrin outlets carry the 'novi glavni izvršni direktor' stories with career-history detail that bank governance pages omit (prior employers, start dates, internal promotion path). Useful as the corroboration layer that dates a leadership move when the bank's own page shows only a current-state roster with no timestamp.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — entity record for Udruženje banaka Crne Gore
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregator carrying UBCG's registered address (Novaka Miloševa bb, Podgorica), founding date (2003-04-07) and contact details — useful for confirming legal identity, the registered representative, and for resolving the association's true web presence. Same pattern applies to every other association in this cell.

source_name: Zakon o mirnom rješavanju radnih sporova (PDF, hosted by Unija poslodavaca CG)
why_relevant: Defines what a collective vs individual labour dispute is, who must file and what is recorded — the legal grammar needed to interpret AMRRS outputs and to know which restructuring events generate a mandatory paper trail.

source_name: ZZZCG — Obavještenje o promjeni u oglašavanju slobodnih radnih mjesta (publication-rules notice)
why_relevant: Documents how and where vacancies must be advertised — indicates publication in the daily newspaper 'Dan' on Mondays/Wednesdays/Fridays plus the ZZZCG website. Establishes the legal/procedural publication venue chain, i.e. tells a collector which off-web channels also carry vacancies and on what cadence.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica - e-banking platform migration notices (Halcom -> eMon OfficeBanking)
why_relevant: Customer-facing migration notices on a private bank's own site are one of the few public disclosures of a supplier swap at a Montenegrin bank (here: away from Halcom's platform to an OfficeBanking-family product). Such projects reliably accompany internal reorganisation and vendor-side hiring.

source_name: IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) — Montenegro
why_relevant: FSAP reports profile supervisory organisation, staffing and governance arrangements of the CBCG in depth; infrequent but the most granular external description of the supervisor's internal structure.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Banking & Finance in Montenegro (comparative guide)
why_relevant: Regional (CEE/SEE) legal-market publisher whose Montenegro banking chapter is authored by local counsel; explains the governance framework (e.g. two-tier management/supervisory board regime) that determines what 'leadership change' filings look like, and identifies law firms advising on the bank M&A deals — a pointer to deal actors.

source_name: Decent Work Balkans – Montenegro Fact Sheet
why_relevant: Regional labour-rights monitoring project publishing country fact sheets on union density, collective bargaining coverage and dispute practice — context for judging how much of a bank's workforce is unionised and therefore how visible a restructuring will be.

source_name: ecoi.net — archived copies of EU/IFI country documents on Montenegro
why_relevant: Stable third-party archive of enlargement reports and related institutional documents, useful when EC URLs rotate between publication cycles and for building a longitudinal series of institutional-capacity assessments.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Report 2025 (SWD(2025) 754 final)
why_relevant: The annual enlargement report assesses Chapter 9 (financial services) and Chapter 4 alignment, the administrative and staffing capacity of the CBCG and supervisory agencies, and flags appointment/independence issues — the authoritative outside account of organisational change in Montenegrin financial institutions.

entity_name: European Parliament report on the Commission reports on Montenegro
source_name: European Parliament report on the Commission reports on Montenegro (A10-0093/2025)
why_relevant: EP rapporteur reports comment on politicised appointments and institutional independence, often naming contested leadership processes at regulators — a complementary, more explicit political read than the Commission's SWD.

source_name: European Western Balkans — accession-monitoring analysis in English
why_relevant: Specialist English outlet that distils each enlargement report and follows appointment/independence controversies at Montenegrin institutions faster than the official documents themselves.

entity_name: Granski kolektivni ugovor za banke, druge finansijske organizacije i osiguranje u Crnoj Gori
source_name: Granski kolektivni ugovor za banke, druge finansijske organizacije i osiguranje u Crnoj Gori (sector collective agreement)
why_relevant: The banking-sector branch collective agreement, signed between the financial-organisations union and Unija poslodavaca. It sets redundancy severance floors (e.g. up to 36 net salaries for long-service staff declared tehnološki višak) and consultation duties — i.e. it defines the cost and the procedure any bank restructuring must follow, and identifies the union counterparty by name.

source_name: Infinum Podgorica office page (tech scaleup office-opening template)
why_relevant: Regional scaleup that opened a Podgorica office with a named managing director — the canonical pattern for how office openings and country-lead appointments are disclosed (company office page + local press), and a template for monitoring similar fintech entrants.

source_name: Law-firm labour-law briefings on Montenegro (Karanović & Partners, BDK Advokati, Schoenherr, Mondaq)
why_relevant: Practitioner commentary on the Labour Act sets out redundancy thresholds, severance floors, consultation duties and the 6-month re-hiring ban — the interpretive layer needed to read bank restructuring announcements and to anticipate cost. Firms also flag amendments in advance of employer behaviour changes.

entity_name: Twinning partner central banks/supervisors publishing on Montenegro
source_name: Twinning partner central banks/supervisors publishing on Montenegro (HNB, Deutsche Bundesbank, BaFin, DNB, HANFA)
why_relevant: Twinning partners publish their own project accounts naming the beneficiary departments, the resident twinning adviser and CBCG counterparts — an external mirror of CBCG organisational reform that local sources often omit.
